mentl/1664757:
The banked m5 probe ran on the saved march artifacts and killed two
stories in one sitting: m4 != m5 (no wash-out), and the same binary
on the same input twice produces DIFFERENT outputs — the free_in_
fields k2 yield-floor staging flips as exactly one bit, everything
else byte-identical. The import census closes clock and random (the
module has neither); differing draws print identical judgment
streams, so the varying read lives in lower's classification after
judgment. The measured lead: the pinned tree peaks at 1.73 GiB and
is stable, the fixed tree at 2.08 GiB and flips — the signed-i32
2^31 boundary sits exactly between them, and every byte address
above it reads negative to a signed compare. Next discriminator:
a trimmed-input compile under the fix held below 2 GiB — flip gone
convicts the boundary (making compress-on-read load-bearing twice);
flip surviving sends the binary-patch probe to the k2 classifier's
input across two draws. Re-land order stands.

mentl/1693ac4:
Previous commit 08a53ef placed the E_RedundantBraces check inside
parse_block_expr — but parse_block_expr is invoked for ALL `{ ... }`
blocks: fn bodies, if-then arms, if-else arms, match arm bodies. So
`if cond { single_expr } else { single_expr }` triggered the warning
on each arm — false positive per SYNTAX.md:1542-1551 where `if cond {
body }` is canonical.

Move the check into a new wrapper parse_block_expr_checked that
parse_body delegates to. parse_body is the fn-body-only entry point
(callers: parse_fn line 392, lambda expression line 921). All other
parse_block_expr call sites (if-arms, match-arm bodies, raw block
expressions) bypass the check.

Added two small projection fns:
  block_stmts_count(node)       — extracts stmts count from a parsed
                                  BlockExpr-shaped Node
  block_expr_stmts_count(e)     — inner match on Expr

Each returns -1 for "not a BlockExpr" (sentinel for "skip check"; the
`stmts.len == 0` predicate rejects -1 so no false positive). The
sentinel here is `0 - 1` not a fabricated value — it's a real number
that the `== 0` check rejects.

Tested:
  T1 multi-line `fn main() = { let x = 1\n 999\n }` → emits 999, NO warning
  T2 single-line `fn main() = 999`                  → emits 999, NO warning
  T3 redundant fn body `fn main() = { 999 }`        → emits 999 + WARNING
  T4 if-arm `if 1 > 0 { 100 } else { 200 }`         → emits 100/200, NO warning
